doc.title: Lee Simpson (founder of Jefferson City Buzzards) Interview, 1948-06-09
doc.interviewee: Lee Simpson (founder of Jefferson City Buzzards)

title: Boiled wine at Louis Lock's house and the dizzy bass drummer
summary: Simpson recalls the club visiting Louis Lock's house on Camp Street, drinking boiled wine, and bass drummer Adam Habs falling down dizzy.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Brother Simpson, did you tell the boys about the terrain we had on the trees these nights? That we went to Brother Lock's house and had some boiled wine, and what happened to our field family when we was coming up Camp Street? How is? We visited our grand morse's house, Mr. Louis Lock. And they had enough of stuff there to float a steamboat. And some of the boys imagined that they were steamboats. And got tanked up. And we had at that time the Burgeon's drum and five-coats from both the members of the Burgeon. And in particular, a man by the name of Adam Habs, who was a member of the club, he was the bass drum player. And he picked the bass drum so much that he got dizzy and fell down. And he had to pick him up and put him in a wagon and bring him home.
That is one of the incidents of the Lock's visit.
